$comment: Which files are the GJC engine, and which files merely share its name prefix.
This is the manifest the extraction follows and the list eslint enforces, so
the boundary that is checked and the boundary that moves cannot drift apart.
A `server/gjc-*` file missing from both lists fails `npm test`: a new file in
the engine's namespace is a decision about what ships closed, and it should
not be possible to make it by accident.
`native/` and `src-tauri/` move wholesale and need no per-file list.

application.server/gjc-worker-client.ts: The application's end of the worker protocol. It runs in the application's process, uses application services, and stays behind when the engine moves.
application.server/gjc-engine-manifest.json: This file. It describes the split for both repositories and belongs to neither exclusively.
application.server/gjc-engine-manifest.test.ts: Keeps this manifest honest against the tree. It describes the split rather than either side of it.
application.server/gjc-live-session-root.test.ts: Asserts where the application looks for live session transcripts, not how the engine writes them.
application.server/gjc-worker-protocol-spec.test.ts: Checks the published protocol specification against the codec. Travels with whichever repository publishes the specification; listed here so the choice is deliberate.
application.server/gjc-herdr-automation-store.ts: Application-owned protected SQLite persistence for managed automation; it depends on the App storage and is not part of the Bun SDK engine.
application.server/gjc-herdr-automation.bun.test.ts: Cross-process managed automation integration exercises the App bridge ledger as well as the SDK; this application contract test stays with the App.
application.server/gjc-herdr-bootstrap.test.ts: Tests App database compatibility and protected launch descriptors before constructing a managed SDK owner.
application.server/gjc-herdr-child-client.ts: The Node application's private transport to the managed Bun child; owns App persistence acknowledgements, not SDK execution.
application.server/gjc-herdr-child-client.test.ts: Verifies application transport correlation, bounded framing and persistence barriers across the managed child boundary.
application.server/gjc-herdr-host-evidence.test.ts: Exercises App-owned protected storage and the automation bridge ledger while retaining a managed SDK continuation.
application.server/gjc-herdr-host-foundations.test.t: Covers managed application host queue, policy, client attachment and snapshot persistence using the App database.
application.server/gjc-herdr-installed-launch.test.t: Verifies the App's installed-application authorization, dispatch and reconciliation with a retained host callback.
Application integration harness for the managed child protocol and retained SDK lifecycle, including App-side admission expectations.
application.server/gjc-herdr-offline-init.bun.test.t: Tests the App's fixed managed Bun entrypoint and offline stored-credential startup contract rather than the runtime package in isolation.
application.server/gjc-herdr-task-console.ts: Human terminal frontend to App-owned host commands and receipts; remains separate from private engine event transport.
application.server/gjc-herdr-task-console.test.ts: Tests the managed App console grammar, bounded input and safe presentation independent of the SDK engine.
application.server/gjc-herdr-task-console-pty.test.t: Verifies the App-owned physical terminal line discipline and independent host/private SDK lifetime through a real PTY.
application.server/gjc-herdr-task-host.ts: Independent Node App host entrypoint owns SQLite, attach clients and launch lifecycle; only its private Bun child belongs to the SDK engine.
application.server/gjc-herdr-task-host.test.ts: Tests App host claims, durable commands and connection lifetime against private child execution.
